summary: Iteration 6 (routing bugfix + public-report tokens/24h-ban) tested. Backend: 8/8 pytest tests pass — routing returns 200 for guwahati->silchar, imphal->agartala, pasighat->aizawl (all previously 404) with LOCAL 'local-*' segments; unknown place returns 400 listing valid places; guwahati->shillong recommended route has no blocked segments (blocked corridor pushed to rejected alternative); public report -> gov verify awards +10 tokens; field officer can verify public reports; public report -> gov reject sets report_ban_until ~24h and further POST /api/public/reports returns 403 'Reporting suspended for 24h...'. Frontend: /routes as logistics operator computed guwahati->silchar (ETA 5h 16m, 210.4 km, risk 25 LOW), 2 UNVERIFIED LOCAL segments listed, map-endpoint-A and map-endpoint-B pins rendered on map, alternative-rejected card shows NH-6 government closure rationale. /public as public user shows public-token-balance chip ('0 tokens') and no ban banner (clean state). Public demo user reset to tokens=0, no ban at end of testing as required.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 715: `contains_blocked = contains_blocked and len(blocked_roads) > 0 or len(blocked_roads) > 0` — operator precedence works but the expression is redundant; simplify to `contains_blocked = len(blocked_roads) > 0`.

_build_graph adds N*3 synthetic local connectors on every /routes/calculate call (recomputed per request). For a demo it is fine, but cache the adjacency graph or memoize by road-status hash to reduce per-request work.

verify_incident/reject_incident: token award and ban writes are not wrapped in a transaction with the incident-status update. If the second write fails, the incident is verified/rejected but tokens/ban never applied. Acceptable for demo, but note for production.

reject_incident sets report_ban_until as string ISO; create_public_report parses it with datetime.fromisoformat and swallows ValueError silently — a malformed value would let a banned user bypass the ban. Consider storing as a proper Mongo datetime.
server.py is now 1371 lines — split into routers (routes.py, incidents.py, public.py) for maintainability.

No GET /api/incidents endpoint exists; incidents are only reachable via /api/dashboard/summary. Frontend/testing convenience suggests adding a dedicated GET /api/incidents with optional status filter.
